property_summary: The reference contract always returns true on successful completion; the mutant returns false, violating the invariant that the return value must be true when all sub-calls succeed.
Calling c.transfer with an empty _tos array must revert; the reference reverts due to require(_tos.length > 0) but the buggy version skips the loop and returns true.
The function transfer must always revert when _tos array is empty and caddress is a contract that would revert on transferFrom; the mutant skips the loop and returns true instead.
The reference contract must revert the entire transaction if any internal transferFrom call fails, but the buggy contract returns true even when a call fails.
A successful call to transfer(...) should never revert, but the mutant always reverts with `require(false)`.
A successful call to transfer() should return true and not revert for any admissible input, but the mutant always reverts.
For any input, the reference transfer returns true; the buggy version returns false when _tos.length > 0.

For any admissible input where _tos array is non-empty and the external call to caddress succeeds, the reference transfer returns true; the buggy version always returns false regardless of external call success, violating the return-value rule.
